No, Bioshock was a story about an objectivist colony, detached from the rest of the world, that was torn apart from within by a civil war. After all of the "normal" people were dead, the 'protagonist' encounters what was left, specifically splicers, Big Brothers, and Little Sisters with the occasional mentally shattered aristocrat for flavor.

If anything, it reinforces the tenet of objectivism that says that we are connected to reality by our perceptions, which means our interpretation of reality will not always be accurate. It's not against objectivism; it's pointing out that there is still a human factor and when the perceptions of two people conflict, the outcome can come to extremes.
